title: Public finance agents strike against centre closure in Rennes

tea.why: Public finance agents are striking against the planned closure of the cheque and fine processing centres in Rennes.
tea.want: Workers demand a bonus for changing jobs and the recognition of difficult working conditions.
tea.changed: Nov 24: Unions stated that about one million cheques worth 150 million euros remain blocked due to the ongoing strike.

summary: Public finance agents in Rennes have been on strike since October 15, protesting the planned closure of the national cheque and fine processing centres. According to reports from franceinfo.fr and 20minutes.fr, the closure affects around forty posts as part of a consolidation strategy by the public finance directorate, which cited a 70 percent drop in cheque usage over the last decade. The strike has left an estimated one million cheques worth approximately 150 million euros blocked, according to the intersyndicale and CGT Finances publiques representatives. The regional directorate of public finances contested these figures, stating the actual backlog is fewer than 300,000 cheques and fewer than 50,000 interbank payment titles, representing under one percent of the DGFIP's total annual volume. Negotiations between the unions and management have not successfully resolved the workers' demands for a job-transition bonus and arduous-work recognition.
response: According to the regional directorate of public finances, the closures are justified by a 70 percent decline in cheque usage over ten years and high unit processing costs. Management contested union figures, stating fewer than 300,000 cheques are blocked.

updates.text: Public finance agents at the Rennes processing centres began their strike.
Unions reported that one million cheques amounting to 150 million euros are currently blocked.
